decisions.decision: next-auth pinned at 5.0.0-beta.32 (Auth.js v5) rather than 4.24.15 stable
decisions.why: T058 needs frontend/src/middleware.ts and T056 needs a server-side session read. v5 is App-Router-native: auth() works in middleware, server components and route handlers. v4 is Pages-Router-first and its App Router gate is the deprecated next-auth/middleware withAuth wrapper. Both declare next ^16 and react ^19 peers, so compatibility is not the differentiator. Risk is bounded by D1: NextAuth verifies nothing, holds no adapter and no session strategy - it is cookie, CSRF and redirect transport only, and the product session table is the sole authority. Frontend npm audit stays at 0 vulnerabilities.
decisions.rejected: next-auth 4.24.15 stable - rejected because reaching App Router middleware through it means depending on a deprecated Pages-Router API for the authentication gate, which is worse standing than a pinned beta in a confined transport role

decisions.decision: The five new tables are OWNED BY lc_migration with explicit grants to lc_auth; only the SECURITY DEFINER functions are OWNED BY lc_auth
decisions.why: data-model.md Roles says lc_auth Owns the five new tables, but every per-entity Grants table in the same document lists privileges GRANTED to lc_auth - which only makes sense if it is a grantee, not the owner. The per-entity tables are the precise statement and the Roles row is loose prose. Function ownership by lc_auth is required and is not loose: resolve_session() is the one function lc_app may EXECUTE, and it only yields lc_auth reach on session if lc_auth owns it. This also follows 0015s precedent (OWNER TO lc_identity_writer on the definer function) and keeps the runtime auth connection unable to DROP or ALTER the tables it reads.
decisions.rejected: Making lc_auth the table owner - rejected because it would let the runtime connection drop authentication tables, and because ownership would make the explicit grants the data model specifies redundant and untestable: auth-grants-lockdown.test.ts asserts what lc_auth was granted, which is vacuous if it owns everything

decisions.decision: Added a seventh column recent_code_digests jsonb to identity_factor, which data-model.md does not list
decisions.why: FR-020 requires a successfully used code be refused anywhere in FR-056 90-second window, and names claim_attempt() as its home. Enforcing that needs memory of which digests were already accepted for at least that window, and none of the six specified columns can hold it - the requirement was unimplementable as written. Placed on identity_factor rather than in a sixth table because data-model.md commits to five new entities and this entity is already described as holding the lockout state, which is the same class of per-identity verification state. Bounded by construction: at most three codes can legitimately be accepted in one window, and every call prunes older entries before appending. Stores digests only, never codes.
decisions.rejected: A sixth used_code table - rejected because it changes the slice shape to store a bounded scrap of data and contradicts the documented five-entity count
